title: vicia sativa f. leganyana
intro: Vicia sativa f. leganyana, commonly known as Hungarian vetch, is a subspecies of vetch, a type of flowering plant in the pea family (Fabaceae). It has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which provide relief from pain, reduce inflammation, and protect against oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of Hungarian vetch include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities. Its health benefits include supporting cardiovascular health, reducing the risk of certain cancers, and alleviating symptoms of menopausal hot flashes.
